stem: A 5-year-old with longstanding motor difficulties and broader developmental concerns needs a structured assessment that gives an overall developmental picture and includes gross and fine motor skills, which tool is most appropriate?

options.text: Bayley Scale of Infant and Toddler Development
Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scales of Intelligence

explanation: Griffiths III is the best fit. It is used from birth to 6 years and provides a broad developmental assessment including gross motor, fine motor and other domains, which matches this child’s needs.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: It is a broad developmental tool appropriate for a 5-year-old, whereas the other options assess narrower domains or different age groups.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because Griffiths III assesses children from birth to 6 years and covers gross motor, fine motor and broader developmental domains
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the Bayley Scale of Infant and Toddler Development is intended for younger children and is not the best match for a 5-year-old
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because ADOS is used to assess autism-related social communication and behaviour rather than provide a broad developmental profile
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the Romberg test is a neurological balance examination, not a developmental assessment tool
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scales of Intelligence focuses on cognitive testing rather than the broad developmental assessment described
